summary: The candidate implements and tests piggyback load reporting on the normal Python generation and embedding paths, including detokenization, multi-tokenizer fanout, HTTP-worker caching, stale rejection, and watch-mode merging. It is only a partial fix because the supported Rust generation egress bypasses the Python consumer and drops the attached load_snapshot field.

tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before reproduction: all four candidate regression tests failed because output collection, HTTP-worker caching, and watch/piggyback arbitration were absent.
44 tests and 19 subtests passed for the candidate's Python-path regression, fanout, and existing load wire coverage.
Independent architecture contract check proved Rust generation egress bypasses the Python detokenizer/HTTP-worker path and RustServer.push_generation does not serialize or consume load_snapshot.

gpu_evidence: Torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2 with HIP 7.2.26015 reported one visible AMD Instinct MI350X. No model workload was needed for the decisive egress-encoding counterexample.
remaining_counterexamples: With Rust generation egress enabled, SchedulerOutputStreamer attaches load_snapshot but sends the payload to RustServer.push_generation; that encoder does not carry or consume load_snapshot, and TokenizerManager.handle_loop is bypassed. The token response therefore does not update the HTTP-worker piggyback cache.
remaining_limitations: The normal Python serving path was validated by focused source-checkout tests, but this independent review did not repeat the candidate author's tiny-model end-to-end serving run because its raw runtime artifacts were not part of the commit.
No multi-rank or multi-node allocation was exercised independently; per-rank merge and fanout behavior is unit-tested.
The visible GPU is an AMD Instinct MI350X. No NVIDIA, CPU-only serving, or distributed architecture was available.
No native C++, HIP, CUDA, or Rust source changed, so a native rebuild was not applicable.
